I've gone through the whole thing hands-on and it does everything we agreed on. Saving a link still pulls in the page's details and lets me fix them; my "read it later" pile shows just the unread ones on their own; tags are the main way I sort things, it suggests ones I've already used, and it won't let me make a near-duplicate like "news" versus "News"; I can archive something so it drops out of my main list and searches but still find it in the archive and bring it back, while deleting stays a deliberate, confirmed, permanent step.

The searching is exactly the behavior I wanted — I can look up a tag with `#`, search an exact phrase in quotes, combine words with and/or/not, and when I quote a word like "NOT" it's treated as plain text instead of a command; and when I fumble a search it tells me plainly what's wrong instead of losing what I typed. Saving a search to reuse works, tidying up a batch at once shows me the exact count and asks me to confirm before anything drastic, and my library is genuinely private — a second account sees nothing of mine and can't reach my links even if it goes looking.

I'm happy — this is the bookmark manager I set out to have. Thank you for building it.

Just one thing to keep on the list for a future round, not for now: I'll eventually want to bring bookmarks in from my browser and take them back out, and maybe keep a saved copy of a page. We agreed those wait, and I'm glad to accept the app as it stands.
